Tomato.description: Warm-season vegetable requiring well-drained loam soil with high organic matter.

stages.action: Sow seeds in nursery beds or seedling trays with coco-peat.
stages.details: Ensure good drainage, protect from direct harsh sun, and maintain optimal moisture.

stages.action: Transplant seedlings to the main field.
stages.details: Space plants 45-60cm apart. Apply light starter irrigation right after planting.

stages.action: Apply NPK 19:19:19 fertilizer near root zone.
stages.details: Combine with weeding and light soil aerating around the base.

stages.action: Stake tomato vines with bamboo poles and remove weeds.
stages.details: Prevents fungal foliar diseases by keeping leaves off moist ground.

stages.action: Apply Potassium-rich fertilizer & spray micronutrients (Boron/Calcium).
stages.details: Monitor closely for fruit borer pest infestation and blossom end rot.

stages.action: Inspect for leaf curl virus, whiteflies, and fruit borers.
stages.details: Use pheromone traps or neem oil spray if threshold exceeded.

stages.action: Pick mature breaker-stage fruits every 3–4 days.
stages.details: Harvest during early morning to preserve freshness and prolong shelf life.

Paddy (Rice).description: Staple wetland cereal crop requiring standing water management and puddle soil prep.

stages.action: Prepare seedbed and sow pre-germinated paddy seeds.
stages.details: Keep nursery bed saturated with water and treat seeds with fungicide.

stages.action: Transplant 2-3 seedlings per hill at 20x15cm spacing.
stages.details: Maintain 2–3 cm standing water in puddled main field.

stages.action: Apply Urea (Nitrogen) top dressing.
stages.details: Drain excess field water 1 day before applying Urea for better absorption.

stages.action: Perform cono-weeding or manual weeding; regulate standing water.
stages.details: Incorporate weeds back into the soil to boost organic matter.

stages.action: Apply MOP (Muriate of Potash) fertilizer.
stages.details: Critical watering window - do not allow field to dry out.

stages.action: Inspect for blast disease and stem borer; keep shallow water layer.
stages.details: Watch out for brown plant hopper (BPH) at base of stems.

stages.action: Harvest when 80-85% of grains turn golden yellow.
stages.details: Drain water 10 days before expected harvest to firm the ground for machinery.

Wheat.description: Cool-season rabi cereal crop that thrives in rich, well-aerated loam.

stages.action: Sow treated certified wheat seeds at 4-5 cm depth using seed drill.
stages.details: Apply basal dose of DAP and Potash during sowing.

stages.action: Provide 1st critical irrigation at Crown Root Initiation stage.
stages.details: Most moisture-critical phase; yield severely drops if missed.

stages.action: Apply 1st split dose of Urea and spray broadleaf herbicide.
stages.details: Remove Phalaris minor (canary grass) and Chenopodium album weeds.

stages.action: Provide 2nd irrigation and inspect for yellow rust or aphids.
stages.details: Foliar spray of propiconazole if yellow powdery streaks appear on leaves.

stages.action: Apply 2nd split dose of Urea and ensure moisture supply.
stages.details: Irrigate gently to prevent lodging due to spring winds.

stages.action: Give final light irrigation during early dough stage.
stages.details: Stop all irrigation when grain enters hard dough stage to enable drying.

stages.action: Combine harvest when grain moisture falls below 14%.
stages.details: Dry harvested grains in sun to 10-12% moisture before storage.

Maize (Corn).description: Versatile warm-weather grain and fodder crop with fast vegetative development.

stages.action: Sow seeds 60cm row-to-row and 20cm plant-to-plant.
stages.details: Apply full P, full K, and 1/3rd of N as basal dose.

stages.action: Apply second split of Nitrogen (Urea) and earth up rows.
stages.details: Scout for Fall Armyworm (FAW) whorl feeding.

stages.action: Provide critical irrigation; avoid water stress during pollination.
stages.details: Moisture deficit now drastically reduces kernel count.

stages.action: Maintain soil moisture and monitor cob borer pests.
stages.details: Nutrients translocate rapidly into kernel starch.

stages.action: Harvest when black layer forms at the tip of the kernel base.
stages.details: Husks turn pale and dry; thresh and sun dry immediately.

Potato.description: Cool-season tuber crop needing loose, friable soil and consistent moisture.

stages.action: Plant sprouted seed tubers in furrows 50-60cm apart.
stages.details: Treat tubers with bio-fungicide to prevent black scurf.

stages.action: Apply light irrigation when shoots emerge uniformly.
stages.details: Avoid heavy flooding to prevent seed tuber rot.

stages.action: Mound soil around stems and apply remaining Nitrogen.
stages.details: Prevents developing tubers from turning green due to sun exposure.

stages.action: Maintain frequent light irrigations and spray protective fungicide.
stages.details: Late blight can decimate foliage rapidly in cool humid weather.

stages.action: Cut top foliage 10-15 days before harvest to harden tuber skin.
stages.details: Stop irrigation completely to dry soil for digging.

stages.action: Carefully dig tubers without bruising; cure in shade for 10 days.
stages.details: Curing heals skin abrasions and prevents storage decay.

Cotton.description: Major commercial fiber crop requiring warm weather, deep black cotton or loamy soil.

stages.action: Dibble delinted seeds at 90x60cm spacing in ridges.
stages.details: Ensure soil moisture is adequate; apply basal dose of DAP and Potash.

stages.action: Remove weeds and apply 1st split of Nitrogen (Urea).
stages.details: Floral bud (square) formation starts; check for sucking pests like jassids.

stages.action: Apply 2nd split of Nitrogen and spray 2% DAP or Potassium Nitrate for boll retention.
stages.details: Water stress at this stage leads to heavy flower drop.

stages.action: Inspect bolls for pink bollworm and spodoptera; deploy pheromone traps.
stages.details: Look for rosette flowers and entrance holes on young bolls.

stages.action: Pick fully opened, clean white cotton bolls in dry sunny weather.
stages.details: Avoid collecting bracts and trash with lint.

stages.action: Complete final picking of opened bolls and shred crop stalks.
stages.details: Shredding stalks breaks the overwintering cycle of pink bollworm.

Soybean.description: High-protein legume and oilseed crop that enriches soil through atmospheric nitrogen fixation.

stages.action: Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture and sow at 45x5cm spacing.
stages.details: Do not sow deeper than 3-4 cm to avoid poor germination.

stages.action: Perform mechanical inter-cultivation or spray post-emergence herbicide.
stages.details: Keep field strictly weed-free during first 30 days.

stages.action: Ensure soil moisture; spray 19:19:19 or bio-stimulant.
stages.details: Check for girdle beetle and tobacco caterpillar infestation.

stages.action: Critical irrigation if rain fails; monitor for pod blight.
stages.details: Moisture stress during pod fill leads to shriveled beans.

stages.action: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and drop off, and pods rattle when shaken.
stages.details: Harvest early morning to prevent pod shattering.

Sugarcane.description: Perennial high-biomass sugar cash crop requiring abundant sunlight and sustained irrigation.

stages.action: Plant two/three bud setts treated with carbendazim in deep furrows.
stages.details: Apply full basal P and 1/3rd K with farmyard manure.

stages.action: Light weeding, hoeing, and initial Nitrogen top dress.
stages.details: Fill gaps if germination count is low.

stages.action: Apply 2nd dose of Nitrogen and build light ridges around canes.
stages.details: Suppresses weeds and supports cane shoots.

stages.action: Apply final Nitrogen & Potash dose; complete deep earthing up.
stages.details: Prevents lodging and suppresses late unproductive tillers.

stages.action: Spread dry sugarcane trash in furrows; monitor for internode borer.
stages.details: Trash mulching conserves precious soil water.

stages.action: Reduce irrigation frequency to encourage sugar concentration in stalks.
stages.details: Test Brix reading with hand refractometer (optimal > 18%).

stages.action: Cut canes flush with ground level to harvest high-sugar bottom stalks.
stages.details: Crush within 24-48 hours to minimize sucrose inversion.

Groundnut (Peanut).description: Valuable subterranean oilseed legume thriving in light sandy loam soil.

stages.action: Sow certified bold kernels treated with Trichoderma at 30x10cm spacing.
stages.details: Soil must be moist and well-tilled for uniform emergence.

stages.action: Manual weeding and blade harrowing to loosen soil crust.
stages.details: Must be completed strictly before peg initiation.

stages.action: Provide light irrigation; DO NOT disturb soil around plants.
stages.details: Pegs penetrate ground to form pods; hoeing now damages pegs.

stages.action: Broadcast 100 kg Gypsum per acre around base and irrigate lightly.
stages.details: Calcium from gypsum ensures well-filled pods and prevents 'pops' (empty shells).

stages.action: Inspect leaves for dark leaf spots (Tikka); spray chlorothalonil if needed.
stages.details: Foliar diseases cause premature leaf drop and reduce kernel weight.

stages.action: Pull plants when inner shell wall turns dark brown; sun dry pods.
stages.details: Dry until pod moisture drops below 9% to prevent aflatoxin mold.

Chickpea (Gram).description: Cool-season major pulse crop requiring well-drained medium-to-heavy soil with residual moisture.

stages.action: Sow deep in moist soil (8-10 cm) to avoid wilt disease.
stages.details: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium and PSB cultures.

stages.action: Pluck top terminal buds to encourage bushy lateral branching.
stages.details: Increases number of flowering branches and pod yield significantly.

stages.action: Provide 1st light irrigation if winter rains fail.
stages.details: Never irrigate at peak flowering, as it induces vegetative surge and flower drop.

stages.action: Install pheromone traps (4-5/acre) and spray neem seed extract or spinosad.
stages.details: Scout for caterpillars chewing into developing pods.

stages.action: Give final light irrigation at early pod fill stage.
stages.details: Ensures plump, well-sized chickpeas.

stages.action: Cut plants when leaves turn straw-yellow and pods are crisp and dry.
stages.details: Thresh and winnow; store in pest-proof gunny bags.

Mustard.description: Cruciferous rabi oilseed crop requiring cool dry weather and bright sunshine.

stages.action: Sow seeds mixed with sand at 4-5 cm depth with line spacing 30-45 cm.
stages.details: Apply full P, full K, and 50% N along with Sulphur (20 kg/acre).

stages.action: Thin seedlings to 10-15 cm within row and irrigate lightly.
stages.details: Thinning prevents overcrowding and stem spindling.

stages.action: Apply remaining Nitrogen (Urea) and give second irrigation.
stages.details: Ensure adequate soil moisture during flowering initiation.

stages.action: Scout for mustard aphids on tender inflorescences; spray imidacloprid if needed.
stages.details: Cloudy humid weather triggers rapid aphid multiplication.

stages.action: Final light watering if soil is dry; monitor for white rust.
stages.details: Oil synthesis peaks during this window.

stages.action: Harvest in early morning when 75% siliquae turn golden yellowish.
stages.details: Harvesting when damp with morning dew avoids pod shattering losses.

Onion.description: Shallow-rooted bulb vegetable requiring frequent irrigation and friable, fertile soil.

stages.action: Sow seeds in raised nursery beds 10cm apart; protect from damping-off.
stages.details: Seedlings take 40-45 days to reach pencil thickness.

stages.action: Transplant seedlings at 15x10cm spacing in flat beds.
stages.details: Trim top 1/3rd of seedling leaves to reduce transplant transpiration shock.

stages.action: Apply 1st split of Nitrogen (Urea) and perform careful manual weeding.
stages.details: Onions have poor canopy competition; keep entirely weed-free.

stages.action: Apply remaining Nitrogen and Potash; inspect leaves for silvery thrips patches.
stages.details: Spray spinosad or neem formulation if thrips colonies spotted.

stages.action: Maintain uniform shallow irrigations; avoid waterlogging.
stages.details: Uneven moisture cycles cause bulb cracking and splitting.

stages.action: Withhold water 10 days before harvest; harvest when 50% tops fall over.
stages.details: Cure bulbs in field shade for 7-10 days to seal neck and maximize storage life.

Chilli (Hot Pepper).description: High-value spice and vegetable crop needing warm sunny weather and pest-managed cultivation.

stages.action: Sow treated hybrid seeds in plug trays with cocopeat and vermicompost.
stages.details: Cover with shade net; maintain fine misting.

stages.action: Transplant seedlings on ridges spaced 60x45cm with basal fertilizer.
stages.details: Irrigate immediately after planting to minimize transplant shock.

stages.action: Apply 1st split of Nitrogen (Urea) and earth up ridges.
stages.details: Check under leaf surfaces for yellow thrips and mites.

stages.action: Foliar spray of micronutrients (Zinc/Boron) & Potassium Nitrate.
stages.details: Prevents flower dropping during sudden temperature spikes.

stages.action: Harvest first flush of shiny green chillies every 7-10 days.
stages.details: Regular picking stimulates new flower flush.

stages.action: Pick fully mature deep-red pods; spread on drying yards.
stages.details: Sun dry until pods rattle with ~10% moisture content.
